lead.t: Skin and soft‑tissue infections (SSTIs) are a spectrum of bacterial, fungal or parasitic conditions that involve the epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, muscle or associated structures, ranging from superficial cellulitis to necrotising fasciitis.

snip.t: Skin and soft‑tissue infections (SSTIs) are a spectrum of bacterial, fungal or parasitic conditions that involve the epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, muscle or associated structures, ranging from superficial cellulitis to necrotising fasciitis.
Pain out of proportion plus a sick patient is necrotising fasciitis until proved otherwise; do not wait for the LRINEC score or imaging.
Skin and soft tissue: Cellulitis, necrotising fasciitis (pain out of proportion), wounds, injection sites
Model Answer: Immediate emergent surgical consultation for operative debridement and source control of necrotising fasciitis.
Deep fascia (Scarpa): Tight, low‑vascular plane – when breached → necrotising fasciitis

Differentials: necrotising fasciitis (pain out of proportion, rapid progression, skin necrosis; see the separate notes), DVT, venous eczema or lipodermatosclerosis, contact dermatitis, gout, erythema nodosum, and drug reactions.
snip.s: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections, and Snake Bites

snip.t: LRINEC score (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotising Fasciitis): CRP (150 mg/L or more = 4 points), WCC (15 to 25: 1; over 25: 2), haemoglobin (11 to 13.5: 1; under 11: 2), sodium (under 135: 2), creatinine (over 141 micromol/L: 2), glucose (over 10 mmol/L: 1).

Differentials: haematoma, seroma, suture reaction, early cellulitis, stitch abscess, necrotising fasciitis (severe pain out of proportion, rapid spread, bullae and crepitus: see the separate notes), and anastomotic leak (for deep-seated infection).
